messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the shedder RFC — I'm worried the current RateLimiter <-> Shedder boundary mixes policy and runtime signals. Thinking we should split out a minimal 'shedder handshake' that only carries admission decision + feedback. Short sketch below, want quick reactions before I write the RFC follow-up.

sanjay: can you sketch the handshake? not convinced we need more indirection.

maya: sketch: 
1) AdmissionRequest { tenant_id, token_count, hints } -> AdmissionDecision { accept | soft-shed | hard-reject, suggested_delay, request_id, epoch }
2) Feedback stream: OnOutcome(request_id, token_count, outcome: success|retry|dropped, latency_ms, abuse_score)
3) Config/Policy: per-tenant static weights + global fallbacks (managed by ops)

elaine: that looks clean. main tradeoff is extra RPC hop adding ~1ms on cold paths, but it gives us the ability to iterate heuristics without touching the RateLimiter core.

kevin: latency seems fine but we need to think about consistency across replicas. If shedder returns soft-shed with suggested_delay, frontends must enforce it. We need idempotency for retries and stable request_id handling.

maya: yep — include request_id + epoch and require frontends to honor the last-epoch decision for a given tenant window. Also allow frontends to cache last-good decision for N ms to avoid hotpath RPCs.

sanjay: can we reuse the existing admission-service v1 API? don't want duplicate endpoints.

elaine: we can reuse the backend but the contract should be intentionally smaller: only admit + feedback. also add a dbg header to force decision mode (for canaries).

rate-bot: shedder-canary deployment 2/3 healthy in us-west-2 :warning:

maya: thanks @rate-bot. rollout plan proposal: 
- dry-run mode on a subset of frontends (local eval)
- canary 5% traffic with dbg header enabled for internal traffic
- 50% traffic with automatic fallback to v1 if soft-shed spike observed
- full switch once metrics stable for 1h
Need a rollback/playbook for ops.

kevin: playbook suggestion: if soft-shed >= 5% of requests for > 10m, auto-failover to v1 and alert SRE. also expose a kill-switch to disable shedder in-flight.

elaine: telemetry requirements: per-tenant soft-shed ratio, avg suggested_delay, top-k tenants by shed rate, and recovered QPS. Also store sample request payloads (redacted) for offline evals.

sanjay: question on abuse signals: should shedder consume raw detector outputs or an aggregated abuse_score? RFC included both options.

maya: prefer a single aggregated abuse_score (0..1) in AdmissionRequest. That keeps the interface stable while detection internals evolve, and we can version the score semantics.

kevin: security note: don't trust client-provided hints. Validate on server-side and cap suggested_delay. Also rate-limit hint frequency.

maya: ops note: canary should pin buckets by tenant (sticky) to avoid noisy neighbors skewing results.

elaine: I'll own telemetry schema and a basic dashboard for the canary.

maya: I'll draft the proto and a short RFC follow-up doc (including rollout checklist).

kevin: I'll own the ops playbook and kill-switch wiring.

sanjay: I'll do a compatibility sweep vs v1 admission API and flag any TODOs.

maya: action items recap: maya(api + follow-up RFC), elaine(telemetry + dash), kevin(playbook + failover), sanjay(compat check). I'll post a proto draft tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
